The first chunk loads the optimization, plotting, data-manipulation, layout, and
project-path packages used below. In particular, CVXR expresses the constrained
least-squares problem, while `here` makes file paths independent of the current
working directory.

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#Load Libraries
library(CVXR)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(patchwork)
library(here)
```

directories for figures, predictions/diagnostics, and saved model objects.
These paths are shared by later chunks; this setup does not alter model data.


This chunk sources the shared plotting helpers and preprocessing/comparison


### Load dataset

For this model, we will use the following training and testing datasets:

* `prediction_dataset.csv`: For prediction purposes

* `regression_dataset.csv`: For training and regression purposes

* `vnm_.csv`: For constraints purposes

All data sets have been cleaned and contain no missing values.

This chunk reads provincial regression observations, level-2 prediction
features, national GDP constraint totals, and provincial 2025 GRDP-per-capita
and population targets. Official population is recorded in thousands, so it is
converted once to persons here to match the prediction data's units.

```{r}
# Regression Dataset
regression_data <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "training_data/regression_dataset.csv"))

# Prediction Dataset
prediction_data <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "training_data/prediction_dataset.csv"))

# National GDP totals used to constrain the regression fit
constrained_data <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "_vnm_indicators/vnm_level0_gdp.csv"))

# Provincial GRDP per-capita targets used to calibrate 2025 level-2 predictions
provincial_grdp_data <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir,
  "_vnm_indicators/vnm_GRDPpc.csv"),
  check.names = FALSE
)

# Provincial population totals (thousands) used as the aggregation constraint
provincial_population_data <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir,
  "_vnm_indicators/vnm_population.csv"),
  check.names = FALSE
)

# Provincial population data are in thousands; convert to persons.
provincial_population_data[, as.character(2020:2025)] <-
  provincial_population_data[, as.character(2020:2025)] * 1000
```

### Shared training and holdout setup

The shared setup converts regression population to persons, splits 2020–2024
from the 2025 holdout, standardizes the common features and outcome using
training-only statistics, applies those transformations to both partitions,
and computes linear temporal extrapolation weights. The native OLS reference
predictions are saved for comparison; the constrained linear fit remains
model-specific.

```{r}
model_setup <- prepare_model_comparison_setup(regression_data)
regression_data <- model_setup$regression_data
training_data <- model_setup$training_data
holdout_data <- model_setup$holdout_data
training_years <- model_setup$training_years
holdout_year <- model_setup$holdout_year
feature_columns <- model_setup$feature_columns
scaled_feature_columns <- model_setup$scaled_feature_columns
feature_means <- model_setup$feature_means
feature_sds <- model_setup$feature_sds
temporal_extrapolation_weights <- model_setup$temporal_extrapolation_weights
ols_comparison <- fit_ols_comparison(model_setup)
ols_reference_predictions <- ols_comparison$holdout
ols_reference_predictions$residual <-
  ols_reference_predictions$actual - ols_reference_predictions$predicted
ols_reference_predictions$residual_scaled <-
  ols_reference_predictions$actual_scaled -
  ols_reference_predictions$predicted_scaled
```


### Preliminaries
Supposed:

* \(y \in \mathbb{R}^n\): observed outcome vector. That is, `grdp_per_capita`.
* \(x_i \in \mathbb{R}^3\): standardized explanatory variables for observation \(i\): `mean_radiance`, `population`, and `pixel_count`.
* \(\alpha_t \in \mathbb{R}\): year-specific intercept for year \(t\).
* \(\beta \in \mathbb{R}^3\): shared slopes for the explanatory variables.
* \(a_t \in \mathbb{R}\): specified national GDP total for year \(t\).

The model includes a separate training-year intercept and shared slopes for the explanatory variables. It is fit on standardized 2020–2024 data only; the population-weighted national GDP constraints apply to those training years. The 2025 holdout is scored against the shared OLS baseline without refitting.

This chunk binds the common training and holdout design matrices and outcomes
to the constrained model's symbols. It also matches national GDP targets to
training years; the subsequent equality constraints use population-weighted
predicted per-capita values to reproduce each matched annual total.

```{r}
# Constrained fitting uses exactly the shared training partition and design.
X <- model_setup$X_train
X_test <- model_setup$X_test
y_train_scaled <- model_setup$y_train
y <- model_setup$y_train_raw
y_test <- model_setup$y_test_raw
training_population <- training_data$population
year <- training_data$year
years <- training_years
population <- training_population
p <- ncol(X)
target_gdp <- constrained_data$gdp[
  match(training_years, constrained_data$year)
]
```

### Optimization problem

Fit only the 2020–2024 training data using the shared standardized response
and design matrix. National GDP constraints are retained for these training
years only; 2025 remains an untouched evaluation partition.
\[
\boxed{ 
\begin{aligned}
\min_{\alpha,\beta}\quad & \|y_{\mathrm{train}}-\hat y_{\mathrm{train}}\|_2^2\\
\text{s.t.}\quad
&\sum_{i:\,\mathrm{year}_i=t} P_i(\bar y+s_y\hat y_i)=a_t,
\quad t\in\{2020,\ldots,2024\},\\
&\hat y_i=\alpha_{\mathrm{year}_i}+x_i^\top\beta
\end{aligned}
}
\]
In this implementation, the optimization variable spans the year-effect and
standardized-feature columns in the common design matrix. The equality
constraints convert standardized fitted values back to original units before
applying population weights. CLARABEL solves this convex quadratic problem;
an unsuccessful solver status stops execution rather than producing a
partial fit.

```{r}
# Define optimization variable
beta <- Variable(p)

# Define standardized fitted values and convert them to GRDP-per-capita units.
y_hat_scaled <- X %*% beta
y_hat <- model_setup$response_mean +
  model_setup$response_sd * y_hat_scaled

# Define the annual GDP constraints for training years only.
constraints <- lapply(seq_along(years), function(i) {
  idx <- which(year == years[i])
  sum_entries(population[idx] * y_hat[idx]) / target_gdp[i] == 1
})

# Define constrained least-squares problem
problem <- Problem(
  Minimize(sum_squares(y_train_scaled - y_hat_scaled)),
  constraints
)

# Solve
result <- solve(problem, solver = "CLARABEL")

# Print results
print(result$status)

if (result$status %in% c("optimal", "optimal_inaccurate")) {
  beta_hat <- value(beta)
  predictions <- as.vector(X %*% beta_hat) *
    model_setup$response_sd + model_setup$response_mean
  holdout_predictions <- as.vector(X_test %*% beta_hat) *
    model_setup$response_sd + model_setup$response_mean
  ols_predictions <- ols_comparison$training$predicted
  ols_holdout_predictions <- ols_comparison$holdout$predicted
  
  # Optimality and Constraints check
  yearly_check <- data.frame(
    year = years,
    predicted_total_grdp = sapply(years, function(t) {
      idx <- which(year == t)
      sum(population[idx] * predictions[idx])
    }),
    target_total_grdp = target_gdp
  )

  yearly_check$difference <-
    yearly_check$predicted_total_grdp -
    yearly_check$target_total_grdp

  print(beta_hat)
  print(yearly_check)
  print(result$value)
  
  # Save fitted model
  fitted_model <- list(
    coefficients = beta_hat,
    variable_names = colnames(X),
    years = training_years,
    response_mean = model_setup$response_mean,
    response_sd = model_setup$response_sd,
    solver = "CLARABEL",
    solver_status = result$status,
    objective_value = result$value
  )
  
  model_path = file.path(model_output_dir, "constrained_linear_model.rds")
  saveRDS(fitted_model, model_path)
  print(paste("Model saved to:", model_path))
  
} else {
  stop(sprintf("Constrained regression failed with solver status: %s", result$status))
}
```


### Statistical Summary

For each split, the response mean and total sum of squares are computed over that split's observed GRDP-per-capita values. The reported comparison table contains training-fit diagnostics and the 2025 holdout scores for both the constrained model and the shared OLS reference.
\[
\bar y = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} y_i,
\qquad
\mathrm{SST} = \sum_{i=1}^{n}(y_i-\bar y)^2.
\]

The coefficient of determination is computed for each model as
\[
R_C^2
= 1-\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}(y_i-\hat y_i^{(C)})^2}{\mathrm{SST}},
\qquad
R_{OLS}^2
= 1-\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}(y_i-\hat y_i^{(OLS)})^2}{\mathrm{SST}}.
\]

The root mean squared error (RMSE), in GRDP-per-capita units, is
\[
\mathrm{RMSE}_C
=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(y_i-\hat y_i^{(C)})^2},
\qquad
\mathrm{RMSE}_{OLS}
=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(y_i-\hat y_i^{(OLS)})^2}.
\]

This chunk calculates residuals and delegates the training/holdout metric
tables and diagnostic CSVs/figures to the shared helper. \(R^2\) uses the
observed outcome variation within each split, while RMSE is reported in
original GRDP-per-capita units; OLS and constrained predictions are compared
on identical rows.

```{r}
constrained_residuals <- y - predictions
ols_residuals <- y - ols_predictions
comparison_metrics <- write_model_comparison_diagnostics(
  model_name = "Constrained linear model",
  training_data = training_data,
  holdout_data = holdout_data,
  training_fitted = predictions,
  holdout_fitted = holdout_predictions,
  ols_training = ols_predictions,
  ols_holdout = ols_holdout_predictions,
  data_output_dir = data_output_dir,
  figure_output_dir = figure_output_dir,
  file_prefix = "linear_model",
  feature_columns = feature_columns
)
holdout_model_stats <- comparison_metrics[
  comparison_metrics$split == "holdout",
  c("model", "R_squared", "RMSE")
]
training_model_stats <- comparison_metrics[
  comparison_metrics$split == "training",
  c("model", "R_squared", "RMSE")
]
print(holdout_model_stats, row.names = FALSE)
```

### Training fit and residual diagnostics

The next chunk records one row per training observation, including actual,
constrained and OLS fitted values, residuals, year, and predictors. It derives
standardized residuals and \(\sqrt{|r_{\mathrm{std}}|}\) for scale-location
diagnostics, then saves the table for reproducibility.

```{r}
# Training diagnostics data frame
training_diagnostics <- data.frame(
  province = training_data$province,
  year = year,
  actual = y,
  constrained_fitted = predictions,
  constrained_residual = constrained_residuals,
  ols_fitted = ols_predictions,
  ols_residual = ols_residuals,
  year_factor = factor(year),
  mean_radiance = training_data$mean_radiance,
  population = population,
  pixel_count = training_data$pixel_count
)

# Calculate standardized residuals
training_diagnostics <- training_diagnostics %>%
  mutate(
    standardized_residual = constrained_residual /
      sd(constrained_residual),
    scale_location = sqrt(abs(standardized_residual))
  )

# Save
write.csv(
  training_diagnostics,
  file.path(data_output_dir, "linear_model_training_fit_diagnostics.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

This chunk plots observed training outcomes against constrained-model and OLS
fitted values. The 45-degree line is the perfect-prediction reference; the
figure is saved and embedded in the report.


The diagnostic panels examine residual patterns against fitted values and predictors, approximate normality, residual spread, and differences across years. 
These are visual checks rather than formal hypothesis tests.
Because the constrained model imposes annual weighted-sum equalities, its residuals are not independent, identically distributed residuals assumed by standard OLS inference.

The following chunk builds those eight complementary plots: constrained and
OLS residual-versus-fitted, a Q-Q plot, scale-location, residuals against each
feature, and residual distributions by year. The population axis is shown on a
log scale to make its wide range readable; these plots diagnose patterns but
do not establish inferential assumptions.

```{r}
# 1. Constrained: residual vs fitted
p1 <- residual_plot(
  training_diagnostics,
  "constrained_fitted", "constrained_residual",
  "Constrained: residual vs fitted",
  "Fitted values", "Constrained residual"
)

# 2. OLS: residual vs fitted
p2 <- residual_plot(
  training_diagnostics,
  "ols_fitted", "ols_residual",
  "OLS: residual vs fitted",
  "OLS fitted values", "OLS residual"
)

# 3. Normal Q-Q plot
p3 <- ggplot(
  training_diagnostics,
  aes(sample = constrained_residual)
) +
  stat_qq(
    color = "#0072B2",
    alpha = 0.65
  ) +
  stat_qq_line(
    color = "#D55E00",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Constrained residual normal Q-Q",
    x = "Theoretical quantiles",
    y = "Sample quantiles"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# 4. Scale-location
p4 <- residual_plot(
  training_diagnostics,
  "constrained_fitted", "scale_location",
  "Constrained: scale-location",
  "Fitted values",
  expression(sqrt("|standardized residual|")),
  zero_line = FALSE
)

# 5. Residual vs radiance
p5 <- residual_plot(
  training_diagnostics,
  "mean_radiance", "constrained_residual",
  "Residual vs radiance",
  "Mean radiance", "Constrained residual"
)

# 6. Residual vs population
p6 <- residual_plot(
  training_diagnostics,
  "population", "constrained_residual",
  "Residual vs population",
  "Population (log scale)", "Constrained residual",
  log_x = TRUE,
  smooth = FALSE
)

# 7. Residual vs pixel count
p7 <- residual_plot(
  training_diagnostics,
  "pixel_count", "constrained_residual",
  "Residual vs pixel count",
  "Pixel count", "Constrained residual"
)

# 8. Residual distribution by year
p8 <- ggplot(
  training_diagnostics,
  aes(x = year_factor, y = constrained_residual)
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    fill = "#B8D8E8",
    color = "#0072B2"
  ) +

    title = "Residual distribution by year",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Constrained residual"
  ) +

# Combine diagnostic plots into a 2 x 4 layout
residual_diagnostics_plot <-
  (p1 | p2 | p3 | p4) /
  (p5 | p6 | p7 | p8) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Training-model assumption checks (visual diagnostics)"
  )

# Save and display
residual_diagnostics_path <- file.path(
  figure_output_dir,
  "linear_model_training_residual_diagnostics.png"
)

ggsave(
  residual_diagnostics_path,
  residual_diagnostics_plot,
  width = 14,
  height = 8,
  dpi = 200
)

knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(residual_diagnostics_path))

```

### 2025 Level-2 Predictions

The first prediction chunk joins each level-2 unit to its provincial 2025
target and population, then standardizes predictors using the training means
and standard deviations. This keeps inference-time feature units consistent
with fitting; it does not recompute scales from prediction observations.

The model first predicts GRDP per capita for each level-2 unit using the 2025 intercept and the same means and standard deviations used to standardize the training data.
Next, we adjust these predictions so that their population weighted total matches the province's reported 2025 GRDP per capita multiplied by its total population.
To do this, we add the same adjustment \(\delta_j\) to every level-2 prediction within province \(j\):

\[ \tilde y_{ij} = \hat y_{ij} + \delta_j \]

The adjustment is calculated as:

\[ \delta_j = \frac{g_jN_j-\sum_{i\in j}P_{ij}\hat y_{ij}} {\sum_{i\in j}P_{ij}} \]

where \(g_j\) is the province's reported GRDP per capita, \(N_j\) is its total population, and \(P_{ij}\) is the population of level-2 unit \(i\).

```{r}
# Prediction adjustment variables
prediction_data$grdp_pc_2025 <- provincial_grdp_data[["2025"]][
  match(prediction_data$level_1, provincial_grdp_data$province)
]

prediction_data$province_population_2025 <- provincial_population_data[["2025"]][
  match(prediction_data$level_1, provincial_population_data$province)
]

# Scale features with the shared training statistics.
for (feature in feature_columns) {
  prediction_data[[paste0(feature, "_scaled")]] <-
    (prediction_data[[feature]] - feature_means[[feature]]) /
    feature_sds[[feature]]
}

# Prediction features
prediction_features <- as.matrix(
  prediction_data[paste0(feature_columns, "_scaled")]
)
```


The final prediction chunk extrapolates year effects to 2025, applies the
fitted coefficients, and adds a common provincial offset \(\delta_j\) so
\(\sum_{i\in j}P_{ij}(\hat y_{ij}+\delta_j)=g_jN_j\). It verifies the
aggregation equality, then writes unit-level predictions and constraint
checks. The offset is population-weighted because every unit in a province
receives the same adjustment.

```{r}
# Extrapolate the fitted year effects to 2025, matching the shared holdout setup.
prediction_X <- cbind(
  matrix(
    rep(temporal_extrapolation_weights, each = nrow(prediction_data)),
    nrow = nrow(prediction_data)
  ),
  as.matrix(prediction_data[paste0(feature_columns, "_scaled")])
)
colnames(prediction_X) <- colnames(model_setup$X_train)

raw_predictions <- as.vector(prediction_X %*% beta_hat) *
  model_setup$response_sd + model_setup$response_mean


# Calculate a common adjustment for each province
province_names <- sort(unique(prediction_data$level_1))

province_adjustments <- setNames(
  numeric(length(province_names)),
  province_names
)

for (province in province_names) {

  # Identify level-2 units within the province
  idx <- which(prediction_data$level_1 == province)

  # Calculate total provincial population from level-2 units
  province_population <- sum(prediction_data$population[idx])

  # Calculate the target provincial GRDP
  target_total <- prediction_data$grdp_pc_2025[idx[1]] *
    province_population

  # Calculate the initial predicted provincial GRDP
  raw_total <- sum(
    prediction_data$population[idx] * raw_predictions[idx]
  )

  # Calculate the common adjustment for all level-2 units
  province_adjustments[province] <-
    (target_total - raw_total) / province_population
}


# Apply provincial adjustments to level-2 predictions
prediction_data$raw_grdp_per_capita <- raw_predictions

prediction_data$province_adjustment <-
  province_adjustments[prediction_data$level_1]

prediction_data$predicted_grdp_per_capita <-
  prediction_data$raw_grdp_per_capita +
  prediction_data$province_adjustment


# Verify provincial calibration
province_check <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  province_names,
  function(province) {

    # Identify level-2 units within the province
    idx <- which(prediction_data$level_1 == province)

    # Calculate provincial population from level-2 units
    province_population <- sum(prediction_data$population[idx])

    # Retrieve the reported provincial GRDP per capita
    target_grdp_per_capita <- prediction_data$grdp_pc_2025[idx[1]]

    # Calculate target and predicted provincial GRDP
    target_total <- target_grdp_per_capita * province_population

    predicted_total <- sum(
      prediction_data$population[idx] *
        prediction_data$predicted_grdp_per_capita[idx]
    )

    data.frame(
      province = province,
      population = province_population,
      target_grdp_per_capita = target_grdp_per_capita,
      predicted_grdp_per_capita = predicted_total / province_population,
      target_total_grdp = target_total,
      predicted_total_grdp = predicted_total,
      difference = predicted_total - target_total
    )
  }
))


# Prepare level-2 prediction results
level2_predictions <- data.frame(
  level_2 = prediction_data$name,
  level_1 = prediction_data$level_1,
  year = prediction_data$year,
  population = prediction_data$population,
  raw_grdp_per_capita = prediction_data$raw_grdp_per_capita,
  province_adjustment = prediction_data$province_adjustment,
  predicted_grdp_per_capita = prediction_data$predicted_grdp_per_capita,
  province_grdp_per_capita_target_2025 = prediction_data$grdp_pc_2025
)


# Save prediction results
prediction_output <- file.path(
  data_output_dir,
  "linear_model_level2_predictions.csv"
)

write.csv(
  level2_predictions,
  prediction_output,
  row.names = FALSE
)


# Display results
print(province_check, row.names = FALSE)

head(level2_predictions)

```
